hero.headline: BigCommerce vs Payhip
hero.subheadline: A side-by-side comparison for buyers, operators, and affiliate-content readers.

summary.winner_hint: Best for scale vs best for creators
summary.best_for_a: BigCommerce is best for merchants who need a scalable, full-featured online store with advanced customization and enterprise-level integrations.
summary.best_for_b: Payhip is best for creators and small sellers who want a simple, low-friction way to sell digital products with built-in affiliate management and fast setup.
summary.quick_take: BigCommerce and Payhip both sell online, but they target different sellers. BigCommerce excels as a robust, scalable e-commerce platform for growing brands that need custom storefronts, advanced checkout options, and wide third-party integration. Payhip is a lean, creator-focused solution that makes selling digital goods, memberships, and subscriptions effortless while including a straightforward affiliate program. Choose BigCommerce for store power and flexibility; choose Payhip for speed, simplicity, and creator-friendly affiliate tools.

rows.tool_a: BigCommerce supports affiliate programs via integrations and apps; flexible but may need setup or partner tools.
rows.tool_b: Payhip includes built-in affiliate management with commission controls, tracking links, and simple payouts out of the box.

rows.tool_a: Requires more time to configure storefront, themes, and integrations—best for merchants who need customization.
rows.tool_b: Quick to start: upload a product, enable affiliates, and share links—ideal for creators and small sellers.

rows.tool_a: Strong support for physical products, variants, subscriptions, and digital products via apps.
rows.tool_b: Designed primarily for digital downloads, memberships, subscriptions, and printables; physical sales are possible but limited.

rows.tool_a: Built to scale from small shops to large enterprises with high traffic and complex catalogs.
rows.tool_b: Best for solo creators and small businesses; not intended for high-volume enterprise catalogs.

rows.tool_a: Tiered subscription model with optional transaction fees depending on gateway; cost increases with growth and add-ons.
rows.tool_b: Simple, low-cost plans with a free tier; Payhip takes small fees on some plans—transparent for creators.

rows.tool_a: Extensive marketplace with payment gateways, ERP, marketing, and shipping integrations.
rows.tool_b: Limited integrations focused on creator tools, email, and analytics—covers essentials but fewer enterprise apps.

rows.tool_a: Full theme control, APIs, and developer tools for tailored storefronts and branded experiences.
rows.tool_b: Minimal customization aimed at fast launches; branding options exist but are constrained.

rows.tool_a: Supports many gateways and region-specific payment options; payout timing depends on gateway.
rows.tool_b: Built-in payout options and simple payment flows oriented toward quick creator payments.

rows.tool_a: 24/7 support on higher plans, developer documentation and professional agency ecosystem.
rows.tool_b: Email support and knowledge base targeted at creators; fast responses but fewer enterprise support options.

rows.tool_a: Brands that need a flexible, scalable storefront, multi-channel selling and advanced commerce features.
rows.tool_b: Independent creators, digital product sellers and educators who want a simple affiliate-ready checkout.

paragraphs: Comparing BigCommerce and Payhip means choosing between a full-featured e-commerce platform and a streamlined creator tool. Both support selling and affiliate programs, but they take different approaches to pricing, product types, and scale.

This comparison highlights the affiliate features, setup time, cost, and where each platform drives the most sales so you can pick the tool that converts buyers and partners efficiently for your business.

data.headline: BigCommerce for growth, Payhip for creators
data.summary: If you prioritize scalability, multi-channel selling, and deep customization, BigCommerce wins. If you want a fast, low-cost way to sell digital products with built-in affiliate tracking and minimal setup, pick Payhip.

items.question: Can BigCommerce run an affiliate program?
items.answer: Yes — BigCommerce supports affiliate programs through third-party apps and integrations or custom solutions; it's flexible but often requires additional setup compared with platforms that include native affiliate tools.

items.question: Does Payhip include affiliate management?
items.answer: Yes — Payhip has built-in affiliate tracking, commission settings, and easy link sharing designed for creators who want a turnkey affiliate solution.

items.question: Which platform is better for selling digital downloads?
items.answer: Payhip is optimized for digital downloads and memberships with immediate delivery and simple pricing, while BigCommerce can sell digital products but shines more for complex storefronts and physical inventory.

items.question: Which option will convert affiliates faster?
items.answer: Payhip often converts affiliates faster because of its simple setup, automatic tracking links, and creator-friendly payouts; BigCommerce can convert high-value partners but usually needs more onboarding and configuration.

items.question: How should I choose between them?
items.answer: Choose BigCommerce if you need scalability, extensive integrations, and full control over your store. Choose Payhip if you prioritize speed, low complexity, and an included affiliate program geared toward creators.
